title: Glass Lung
description: Ultimate Beat Battle Round 1 (Opus). A 2-step garage miniature in C# minor at 140 BPM: one synthetic singer heard an octave down through a wall, then in her real register over the beat; a monophonic 808 made from three choked voices; GLASSHOUSE glass answering the hook.

tracks.description: The hook: synthetic vowel syllables sung on G#4, pitched per note with playbackRate.

patterns.description: Hook statements bars 3-8 and 13-16; bar 8 stutter; bar 15 suspension bend; bar 16 tape stop.

tracks.description: The hook an octave down: dark, slowed-tape version for the intro, breakdown answers and outro.
Breakdown call phrases (answered by vox-low) and the final-drop harmony a diatonic third below.
Tape spin-up riser (0.25 -> 1 over six beats) and an inhale filling the last beat of silence before bar 13.
GM electric piano: rootless voice-led chords, 2-step stabs in the drops, held in the switch.
Intro chords, low-passed at 700 Hz like a room next door.
GM choir aahs: a human halo behind the synthetic voice in the switch and final drop.
GLASSHOUSE glass-hit retuned per note: answers to the hook and a final-drop counter-line.
Reverse glass (two beats) into bars 5 and 13; prism impacts on 13:1 and the final downbeat (slowing to half speed).
2-step kick: 1 and the and-of-3, with a swung ghost and pickup on alternate bars.
Clap on 2 and 4 in the drops, half-time on 3 in the switch.
Swung offbeat hats, rims answering the vocal, shaker in the switch, rising snare roll in the build.
808 voice 1 of 3 (round robin); gain automation chokes each note when the next one starts.
808 voice 2 of 3 (round robin); gain automation chokes each note when the next one starts.
808 voice 3 of 3 (round robin); gain automation chokes each note when the next one starts.
